entries.name: Norse / Vikings (Viking Age Scandinavians)
entries.settlement: longhouse farms along fjords and coasts; trading towns like Hedeby, Birka and Kaupang
trade: slaves, furs, amber and walrus ivory out
entries.beliefs: Norse paganism (Odin, Thor, Freyja); gradually Christianized from the 10th century
entries.fell_by: Christianization and rival kingdoms; absorbed into Denmark, Norway and Sweden
entries.notes: The archetypal sea-raider culture. Play them as seasonal traders-raiders, not constant war; the longship is the unit of history.

entries.name: Anglo-Saxons
entries.settlement: nucleated villages; later defended burhs under Wessex
crafts: gold filigree and garnet cloisonne (Sutton Hoo)
entries.beliefs: Germanic paganism, then Christianity from Rome and from Iona
entries.fell_by: Norman conquest, 1066
entries.notes: Heptarchy of small kingdoms, unified by Alfred and his heirs. Bede and Beowulf are the best windows into them.

entries.name: Franks (Merovingian and Carolingian)
entries.region: Gaul and the Rhine (later France and Germany)
entries.settlement: royal villas and walled towns; monastery-led expansion
entries.beliefs: Germanic paganism, then Catholic Christianity (Clovis baptized c. 496)
entries.fell_by: Treaty of Verdun 843 split the realm into what became France and Germany
entries.notes: The bridge from Rome to the medieval world; Charlemagne rebuilt a west-European empire.

entries.name: Celts (Hallstatt and La Tene)
entries.settlement: hillforts (Dun Aengus style) and later oppida trading towns
crafts: enamel and La Tene curvilinear art
entries.beliefs: Polytheistic; druid priesthood; sacred groves
entries.fell_by: Roman conquest, then Germanic migrations and slow assimilation
entries.notes: Not one tribe: a cultural sphere from Ireland to Anatolia (the Galatians). The -rix name-ending means king.

entries.name: Gauls
entries.settlement: walled oppida and villages; Alesia was the decisive hillfort
trade: grain, salted pork and slaves out
Italian wine and luxury goods in
entries.beliefs: Gaulish pantheon; druids; sacred groves and springs
entries.fell_by: Roman conquest 58-50 BCE (Caesar)
entries.notes: The Gallic War made Caesar's career; Asterix is a loving caricature of them.

entries.name: Brythonic Britons (ancestors of the Welsh, Cornish and Cumbric)
entries.settlement: hillforts, then Romano-British towns with villas and baths
entries.beliefs: Celtic polytheism, then Christianity (by c. 300 CE in some regions)
entries.fell_by: Anglo-Saxon migration and settlement, 5th-7th centuries
entries.notes: Arthur is likely a composite of British war leaders like Ambrosius and Urien; the Welsh language is their direct heir.

entries.name: Gaels (Irish, Scots and Manx)
entries.region: Ireland, western Scotland, Isle of Man
entries.settlement: ringforts and crannogs; later monasteries as power centers
entries.beliefs: Celtic polytheism, then a distinctly Irish Christianity (high crosses, penitentials)
entries.fell_by: never fell; language still spoken in Ireland and Scotland
entries.notes: The early medieval west's scholarship engine; Iona, Kells and Lindisfarne.

entries.name: Normans
entries.settlement: motte-and-bailey castles, then stone keeps; abbey-ruled towns
trade: English silver and Mediterranean goods in
entries.beliefs: Catholic Christianity, militant
entries.fell_by: lost Normandy 1204; merged into England, France and Sicily
entries.notes: Viking grandsons who conquered England, southern Italy and nearly the Holy Land in two generations.

entries.name: Basques
entries.settlement: dispersed farmsteads and fishing ports
trade: cod, whale oil and iron out
entries.beliefs: Indigenous deities (Mari) before Christianity; shepherding rituals; Catholic later
entries.fell_by: never fell; the only pre-Indo-European language in western Europe survives
entries.notes: The language island: whatever the Vascones were, they were on the Pyrenees before Indo-European arrived.

entries.name: Bretons
entries.settlement: villages around parish churches; maritime ports
entries.beliefs: Catholicism with Celtic saint cults (pardons, sacred wells)
entries.fell_by: never fell; united to France 1532, Celtic language and identity persist
entries.notes: Britons who crossed the Channel as the Saxons advanced; the last Gauls to stay Celtic.

entries.name: Sami
entries.settlement: seasonal siida camps; later permanent villages along rivers
crafts: duodji (reindeer hide, antler carving, birch root)
trade: reindeer products, furs and fish out
entries.beliefs: Shamanism (noaidi); later Laestadian Lutheranism
entries.fell_by: never fell; herding communities in Norway, Sweden, Finland and Russia
entries.notes: Europe's indigenous arctic people; Tacitus's Fenni. The only native reindeer herders in the world.

entries.name: Baltic Finns (Finns and Karelians)
entries.settlement: forest farms and log villages; later tar-burning clearings (kaski)
entries.beliefs: Finnic paganism (Ukko); later Lutheran in the west, Orthodox in Karelia
entries.fell_by: never fell; Finland and Karelia keep the language
entries.notes: The Kalevala - Europe's last great oral epic - was sung into a text by Elias Lonnrot in 1835.

entries.name: Frisians
entries.settlement: terp wierden mounds above the marsh coast
entries.beliefs: Germanic paganism, then Christianity (Willibrord, 7th century); later 'Frisian Freedom'
entries.fell_by: never fell; language survives in Fryslan
entries.notes: Once a North Sea naval power (Greater Frisia); after Radbod fell, they vanished from war and into dairy.

entries.name: Picts
entries.settlement: small fortified farmsteads and royal duns
crafts: Pictish symbol stones (inscriptions we cannot read)
entries.beliefs: Indigenous traditions, then Christianity (monasteries like Rosemarkie)
entries.fell_by: merged into the Gaelic Kingdom of Alba (Scotland), c. 900-1000
entries.notes: The 'painted people' of Roman sources; their carved symbol stones are unread books.

entries.name: Gallo-Romans
entries.settlement: Roman towns (Lutetia, Lugdunum) and villas with mosaics
entries.beliefs: Greco-Roman gods syncretized with Gaulish ones, then Christianity
entries.fell_by: Frankish kingdoms; Gallo-Latin shifted into Old French
entries.notes: The people who made Latin into French; the third ingredient in France after Gauls and Franks.

entries.name: Burgundians
entries.settlement: walled towns (Geneva, Lyon) and villas
entries.beliefs: Arian Christianity, later Catholic (Sigismund, 516)
entries.fell_by: Frankish conquest 534; the name survives as the French province of Burgundy
entries.notes: Roots of the Nibelung legend and of Burgundy's wine culture; a Germanic kingdom that Romanized.

entries.name: Old Saxons (continental)
entries.settlement: dispersed farmsteads in loose Saxon federation
crafts: pagan worship at the Irminsul pillar
trade: slaves out (to the Slavic and Muslim world)
entries.beliefs: Germanic paganism (Irminsul, sacred oak); forcible conversion by Charlemagne
entries.fell_by: Charlemagne's wars 772-804; Verden massacre 782, forcible baptism
entries.notes: Charlemagne fought them for thirty years and baptized them at swordpoint; their rebellion is Widukind's legend.

entries.name: Batavians
entries.settlement: farmsteads on river levees
entries.beliefs: Germanic polytheism; veneration of Thincsus (a Thing god)
entries.fell_by: dissolved into the Roman Rhine frontier; name survives as 'Batavia' (old name for the Dutch East Indies)
entries.notes: Tacitus says they were Rome's bravest auxiliaries - and they revolted in 69-70 CE under Julius Civilis.

entries.name: Jutes
entries.region: Kent and the Isle of Wight (England)
entries.settlement: Jutish kingdom of Kent, centered on Canterbury
entries.beliefs: Germanic paganism, then Christianity (Augustine at Canterbury, 597)
entries.fell_by: absorbed into Anglo-Saxon England
entries.notes: The third and smallest of the founding Germanic peoples of England; their tradition says Kent was founded by the brothers Hengest and Horsa.

entries.name: Hallstatt culture (early Celts)
entries.settlement: salt mines and princely hillforts (Heuneburg)
entries.beliefs: Ancestors of Celtic religion; rich princely tombs (Vix krater)
entries.fell_by: evolved into La Tene culture
entries.notes: Salt made them rich; the mine at Hallstatt is the eponym - 'Celts before the name'.

entries.name: Icelandic Commonwealth (Saga Age)
entries.settlement: dispersed farms; thing-steads (Althing from 930); no towns until the 18th century
crafts: saga literature (Snorri, the Sagas of Icelanders)
entries.beliefs: Norse paganism, then Christianity (1000) in a managed coexistence
entries.fell_by: Norway annexed Iceland by the Old Covenant 1262; culture persisted through poverty
entries.notes: The world's purest living Norse saga culture; names like Snorri and Egill are the novelists of the north.

entries.name: Norse-Gaels (Vikings of Ireland)
entries.settlement: walled trading towns at Dublin, Waterford, Limerick and Wexford; later rural Hiberno-Norse farms
entries.beliefs: Norse paganism mixed with Irish Christianity after c. 900
entries.fell_by: Anglo-Norman invasion 1169; dissolved into Gaelic Ireland
entries.notes: Half Viking, half Gael; they founded Dublin and the other Irish port towns. Their kings had names like Olaf and Sihtric.

entries.name: Varangians / Rus'
entries.region: Eastern Europe river routes (later Ukraine and Russia)
entries.settlement: river fort towns (Novgorod, Kyiv) along Volkhov, Dnieper and Volga
trade: furs and slaves out (to Byzantium and Baghdad)
entries.beliefs: Norse paganism, then Orthodox Christianity (988)
entries.fell_by: assimilated by the Slavic majority; 'Rus'' gave Russia, Ukraine and Ruthenia their names
entries.notes: The eastern half of the Viking Age's trade empire; Byzantium hired them as the Varangian Guard.

entries.name: Geats
entries.settlement: small kingdoms around a royal hall (the Heorot of Beowulf's world)
entries.beliefs: Norse paganism
entries.fell_by: absorbed into Sweden; remembered through Beowulf
entries.notes: The Beowulf people. Hygelac died raiding Frisia c. 521 (attested by Gregory of Tours).

entries.name: Hiberno-Scottish monks (Celtic Church)
entries.settlement: monasteries in remote islands (Iona, Lindisfarne, Skellig Michael)
crafts: illuminated manuscripts (Book of Kells, Lindisfarne Gospels)
trade: manuscripts and religious ideas west and east
entries.beliefs: Christianity with an Irish flavor (penitentials, Celtic tonsure, peregrini)
entries.fell_by: Benedictine reform and papal standardization; Viking raids sacked Lindisfarne (793) and Iona (802, 806)
entries.notes: They re-lit learning for Europe after Rome fell; the Vikings nearly burned it all down.

entries.name: Greenland Norse
entries.settlement: two small fjord settlements (Eastern and Western), never much more than a hundred farms
trade: walrus ivory and polar bear skins out
entries.beliefs: Norse Christianity (Brattahlid was Erik the Red's home parish)
entries.fell_by: cold climate, famine, Inuit competition and Norwegian/Danish neglect; last written record 1408 (Hvalsey wedding)
entries.notes: The most famous climate-driven collapse in the north; a warning written in turf and ivory.

entries.name: Bell Beaker culture
entries.settlement: scattered farmsteads; burial mounds
entries.fell_by: evolved into the Bronze Age cultures
entries.notes: Their DNA spread through western European men; the Amesbury Archer was almost certainly an immigrant from continental Europe.

entries.name: Corded Ware culture (Battle-Axe culture)
entries.region: Northern and Central Europe (Sweden to Ukraine)
entries.settlement: small farms; single graves under mounds
entries.fell_by: absorbed into early Bronze Age cultures; likely vector of Indo-European speech into Scandinavia
entries.notes: Whoever they were, they probably brought Indo-European languages to the north.

entries.name: Atlantic megalith builders (Neolithic megalithic culture)
entries.settlement: small farming villages; monumental cemeteries
entries.beliefs: ancestor veneration; solstice-aligned passage tombs
entries.fell_by: replaced by Beaker and Corded Ware immigrants
entries.notes: Newgrange (c. 3200 BCE) predates the pyramids at Giza; we do not know what they called themselves.

entries.name: Nordic Bronze Age
entries.settlement: farms; rock carving sites along coasts (Tanum, Sweden)
entries.beliefs: solar worship (sun chariot, bronze lurs); sea-faring religion
entries.fell_by: Iron Age expansion; evolved into Germanic tribes
entries.notes: Their rock art of ships, sun wheels and ploughs is the root of Germanic Scandinavian culture.

entries.name: Magdalenian culture
entries.settlement: caves and open-air camps at reindeer crossings and salmon rivers
crafts: bone and antler carving (batons de commandement)
trade: long-distance exchange of shells and exotic stone
entries.fell_by: warming climate after the Last Glacial Maximum; reindeer shifted north; evolved into Azilian
entries.notes: The high point of Ice Age art; Lascaux's Hall of the Bulls. The name comes from Abri de la Madeleine.
